+## Maven
+
+The `maven` module indicates the presence of a Maven project in the current directory. If the [Maven Wrapper](https://maven.apache.org/wrapper/) is enabled, the Maven version will be parsed from `.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties` and shown.
+
+By default the module will be shown if any of the following conditions are met:
+
+- The current directory contains a `pom.xml` file.
+- The current directory contains a `.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties` file.
+
+If you use an alternate POM syntax (for example `pom.hocon`), add its filename to `detect_files`.
+
+### Options
+
+| Option           | Default                              | Description                                                               |
+| ---------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `format`         | `'via [$symbol($version )]($style)'` | The format for the module.                                                |
+| `version_format` | `'v${raw}'`                          | The version format. Available vars are `raw`, `major`, `minor`, & `patch` |
+| `symbol`         | `'🅼 '`                               | A format string representing the symbol of Maven.                         |
+| `detect_files`   | `['pom.xml']`                        | Which filenames should trigger this module.                               |
+| `detect_folders` | `['.mvn']`                           | Which folders should trigger this module.                                 |

Please handle `is_maven_project` first for performance. Running this early also diverges from the `gradle` behaviour. If you are planning to keep it this way please add a `TODO` comment to the gradle module to streamline them in the future.

Another potential alternative would be to conditionally handle `is_maven_project` with `begin_ancestor_scan` depending on the value of `upwards` (only using the config options), giving users more control.
I think it would be more reliable to use the `/3.9.12/` part of the url.

OK, but note that this doesn't appear to work:

```rs
            .begin_ancestor_scan()
            .set_files(&[".mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties"])
            .scan()
```

I'll just look for the `.mvn` folder instead, but it would be handy if I could scan for a full relative path.

Any reason? A regex would have to account for various suffixes like `-SNAPSHOT` and whatever else might be possible. On the Gradle side, this approach has worked well for me, including for oddball use cases like custom Gradle distributions with non-standard version numbers.
